newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ten seamen missing after S.Korean ship capsizes.
newsitem.headline: Ten seamen missing after S.Korean ship capsizes.

text.p: Ten seamen were missing and feared dead when a South Korean ship carrying a highly flammable chemical and liquified petroleum gas capsized off the southwest coast of Korea on Sunday, police said.

They said one person, an engineer, had been rescued from the 990 deadweight tonne vessel owned by a shipping company based in the southern port of Pusan. All crew members were South Koreans, they said.
Police in Chindo said the ship capsized after hitting rocks and was now lying partially submerged in the water with only its bow visible.
The coast guard has banned all shipping within a two-mile (3.2 km) radius of the capsized vessel in fear of an explosion.
Ten coast guard vessels and a helicopter were trying to rescue the crew believed to be trapped inside the ship and feared dead from gas fumes, police said.
They said the vessel, the Chuk-yang-ho, was returning from Japan and heading to the port of Kunsan when it capsized.
Police said weather off the coast this morning was clear and waves were low.
